title: Dedicated fleet incident: throughput contract breach, autoscaler regression forensics and remediation sprint
creator: Ariana Patel
description:
Summary:
On 2026-02-18 a sustained throughput regression was detected for multiple Dedicated pools causing customer-visible latency increases and dropped SLA guarantees. Initial alerts were SLO breach pages for 95th percentile latency followed by throttling events in per-tenant queues. Scope: 6 dedicated pools across us-west and eu-west; affected customers: 3 enterprise tenants with reserved throughput contracts.

Hypothesis and root-cause (working):
1) A scheduler refactor (merged in runtime-1.18 candidate branch) adjusted distribution heuristics for batching and kernel selection. For mixed short/long prompt workloads the new heuristic reduced effective batch sizes for tail requests, increasing token latency and backpressure.
2) The autoscaler relies on a short-lived throughput signal that was smoothed by the old dispatcher; after the refactor the signal underestimates transient load leading to delayed scale-ups.
3) Combined, these changes let queues fill and the dedicated-fleet headroom contract be consumed faster than provisioning could restore, triggering per-tenant emergency throttles and SLA breach.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- 2026-02-18 02:13 UTC: Enabled emergency headroom override for impacted dedicated pools (+20% capacity) via fleet-control CLI (manual uplift).
- Rolled back runtime scheduler refactor on us-west and eu-west pools to restore previous batching behavior (partial rollback, tagged runtime-1.17-hotfix).
- Applied temporary per-tenant backpressure rules to even traffic distribution and reduced customer-facing throttling.
- Provisioned short-term hosted burst capacity for the three affected enterprise tenants with contractual comms.

Telemetry gaps discovered:
- Autoscaler telemetry uses 10s windows and loses visibility into 30–90s surge patterns; we lack token-level kernel selection tracing in production by default.
- No deterministic e2e test validates autoscaler decisions under heterogeneous sequence-length mixes.

Known risks and trade-offs of mitigation:
- Manual headroom increases raise short-term cost and reduce available capacity for other customers; applied only to impacted dedicated pools with finance/CS notified.
- Rollback of scheduler reduces medium-term throughput improvements; maintains SLA while we investigate safer patch.
updates: 2026-02-18: 01:58 UTC — SLO alert triggered for 95th percentile token latency on pool-ded-usw-3; paging on-call.
2026-02-18: 02:10 UTC — Triage concluded high queue length + increased per-token latency. Enabled emergency headroom override for impacted pools.
2026-02-18: 03:05 UTC — Rolled back scheduler refactor on two impacted clusters; latency improved ~30% for median, 95th reduced to within SLO for rolled-back clusters.
2026-02-19: 10:20 UTC — Customer success contacted three enterprise tenants; arranged hosted burst capacity and provided incident summary.
2026-02-21: 15:40 UTC — Began controlled canary of an instrumented scheduler patch (adds sequence-length-aware batching counters) in a non-production dedicated cluster.
2026-02-25: 09:04 UTC — Observability sprint started: add per-kernel latency, batch-size-distribution, and autoscaler decision trace logs.
2026-03-01: 13:12 UTC — Preliminary forensics report drafted, signaling autoscaler smoothing window mismatch as leading candidate. Shared with Reliability WG.
2026-03-05: 11:30 UTC — Decision: proceed with two-phase remediation (telemetry + safer scheduler patch + autoscaler integration tests). Assigned remediation sprint.
action_items: Telemetry: instrument per-request kernel selection, batch size, and per-token latency; export to long-term buckets for 90 days. (owner: SRE)
Autoscaler: update signal windowing logic to capture 30–90s surge patterns and add decay hysteresis; add unit and integration tests. (owner: Platform)
E2E tests: add deterministic workload generator that mixes short/long sequences to validate batching heuristics under load. (owner: Runtime)
Rollout policy: implement canary weight decay and automatic rollback when 95th percentile token latency increases >20% in canary. (owner: Deployments)
Operational: update Dedicated runbook to include emergency headroom steps and cost-approval flow; add per-tenant throttling checklist. (owner: Ops)
Customer comms: produce a postmortem for impacted tenants and offer one-week discounted reserved credit as remediation. (owner: CS)
